The interface of interconnected W matrix as evident from SEM micrograph of sintered alloys (Fig. 14, Fig. 15) provides easy path for crack propagation leading to intergranular fracture and suggest low grain boundary strength as compared W matrix.
The fracture is mixed mode (both transgranular and intergranular), however, fracture along the interface is more intense as compared to cracking inside the particles.
The severity of intergranular cracking is comparatively less at 1500 °C and evidence of microvoid formation is present in alloy A indicates ductile fracture.
Evidence of particle shearing and cleavage facets directs towards occurrence of brittle fracture along certain crystal planes .

The strengthening effect in the alloys is resulted from the finer W grains, presence of hard phases at the interface and inside the W matrix as well as solid solution strengthening effect .

Y2O3 dispersed W -Ni alloy exhibit superior densification, hardness and strength owing to enhanced fraction of finer grains (enriched grain boundary diffusion), solid solution strengthening and dispersion strengthening (grain boundary pinning) as compared to Al2O3, La2O3 dispersed W-Ni alloy at all sintering temperature.
The oxide phases induce interfacial pinning and reduce the grain boundary migration and encourage the strengthening of matrix.
The Ni base d liquid phase formation also increases with sintering temperature and imparts higher capillary force and mass transport rate along with pore filling phenomenon.
